lede: Gold jumped about 2.4% on Friday and the S&P 500 logged its best week since April 2025 in a holiday-shortened session, while the dollar firmed after soft eurozone inflation. Bitcoin fell back below $60,000 after a large options expiry, capping a November on course for its steepest monthly drop in over four years.
snapshot_time: Fri 27 Nov close · FX & gold closed for the weekend

focus.text: Rebounded 2.4% Friday to about 3,654 (+3.3% on the week) after Wednesday's one-year low near 3,426. Opens Monday above its 3,631.8 pivot; Tuesday's ISM is the first big risk.
Slipped 0.35% to 1.0936 as softer French and Spanish inflation and weak sentiment data weighed. No pivot confirmed; US ISM and eurozone data next week are the risks.

technicals.indicators: 20- and 50-day MAs still sloping lower · Monday pivot 3,631.8 · Friday range 3,556–3,685
technicals.note: Friday's sharp rebound from the one-year low left a V-shaped recovery inside a falling trend, with 3,750 the next resistance analysts cite and 3,500 the floor below.

technicals.indicators: MACD near the zero line · Stochastic neutral (~50) · down about 1.7% in November
technicals.note: The pair fell back toward the lower end of its recent range after failing below 1.10, with 1.0874 the last swing low on the chart.

technicals.indicators: RSI(14) ≈ 26 (oversold) · below 200-week SMA (≈68,360) · lower Bollinger band ≈54,190
technicals.note: Price rejected near 62,250 on Friday and slipped back under the 61,270 weekly open, keeping the daily structure of lower highs intact.

technicals.indicators: RSI(14) ≈ 28 (oversold) · former support at 1,664 now acting as resistance
technicals.note: Ether lost the 1,664 area overnight, turning it into resistance, with the 21 Nov low near 1,538 the last major support below.

news.text: S&P 500 rose 1.6% to 7,297.49 in Friday's half-day, its best week since April 2025; the Nasdaq added 2.3% as chip and AI names rebounded.
The Fed's pre-meeting blackout has begun with markets pricing a 25bp hike on 9 Dec at roughly 93–100%; the US 10-year yield ended near 4.9%.
Brent settled 1.2% lower at $95.44 but gained about 3% on the week, its first weekly rise in November, as Houthi strikes on Saudi facilities kept supply fears alive.
Ministers meet Sunday; delegates indicate first-quarter 2027 output targets will stay unchanged, while Iraq seeks a higher production ceiling.
French CPI (3.2% vs 3.6% expected) and Spanish HICP (4.1% vs 4.9%) undershot, and the euro-area sentiment index fell to a five-month low.
About $6.75B of bitcoin options expired on Deribit Friday with max pain at $70K; BTC swung from near $62,250 to about $58,760 after the US open.
Bitcoin is down roughly 21–23% in November from a $77.6K open, on track for its biggest monthly fall in more than four years.
US spot bitcoin ETFs have shed a record $5.39B this month through 25 Nov, while ether funds lost about $1.30B; Thanksgiving-week data resumes Monday.
The Fear & Greed index sits at 12, extreme fear; CryptoQuant flags a large pocket of short positions between $60K and $100K.
KuCoin said it will delist Monero spot pairs, Moscow Exchange plans to open crypto trading on 1 Dec, and Binance Blockchain Week runs in Bangkok this weekend.
GraniteShares launched two 3x leveraged XRP ETFs, and Ethereum developers scheduled a December test for the Glamsterdam upgrade.
